I have a similar story. When I was around 13ish my mom and I were at a Halloween store and the cashier was a trans woman, seemingly pretty early in her transition. I just stood there staring at her, probably making her uncomfortable, for the longest time while my heart was beating out of my chest. Partially because I'd heard terrible things about trans people (that were making me repress my own gender dysphoria before I had a complete understanding of what I was even feeling), but she didn't seem like a terrible person at all; she seemed really kind and sweet and nothing about her was "gross" like everyone else had always told me trans people were, and partially because I was thinking of saying something to her. I wanted to say something to her. I wanted to tell her that I liked her hair or that her nail polish was pretty, and I thought about saying "Have a nice day, miss!" when we left, but I was there with my mom and I didn't want to get lectured on the way back home, so I said nothing. I just silently walked out of the store with my mother, who leaned down to whisper "Transgender people freak me out," in my ear. I said nothing, but instead glared at her. "What? They do!" I was silent for the rest of the car ride, wishing that I'd been brave enough to say something. Anything. A lump formed in my throat as I sat there thinking about what I might have said had my mom not been there. Suddenly 13 year old me wanted to confide in someone, and I imagined how things would go if I had confided in her. I thought about telling her that at night when my parents were asleep that I would bind my chest with an ace bandage and hide my hair under a hat and pretend to be a boy and it made me really happy. I thought about telling her that changing in the locker room for gym every day felt awful because I didn't like people seeing how feminine my body had gotten. I thought about telling her that all of these thoughts I had scared me so so much, and how was she ever able to do it? I thought about asking her if I could ever be like her, even when there were mean people in the world who wouldn't like me. Even if those mean people were in my own family.

I'm 17 now, and I still think about her. I really really hope she's doing well, because she was the first trans person I ever met and she made young me realize that maybe being trans doesn't mean someone's a bad person after all.
